```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", dpi = 110)
has_screp <- requireNamespace("scRepertoire", quietly = TRUE)
library(tcrhex)
library(ggplot2)
```

`tcrhex` turns single-cell TCR metadata into "paired TCRdist hex rows". Each
row is one query TCR. Along the row, the clones of your dataset are binned by
their paired TCRdist to the query and drawn as small hexagons coloured by any
categorical column.

This vignette uses the public example data shipped with scRepertoire
(`contig_list`: 8 samples, 4 patients with acute respiratory distress, blood
"B" and lung "L"). The HLA section uses the package's **synthetic** cells.

## 1. Read cells

Every reader returns the same cell table: `cell`, `donor`, `va`, `ca`, `vb`,
`cb`, plus all your metadata columns. A donor (person) is the only required
metadata. Cells with two chains of one locus keep the chain with most UMIs,
and the readers report how many such cells there were. Unpaired cells are
kept, because they count for `top_public()`, but they cannot enter paired
TCRdist.

```{r read, eval = has_screp}
data("contig_list", package = "scRepertoire")
samples <- c("P17B", "P17L", "P18B", "P18L", "P19B", "P19L", "P20B", "P20L")
meta <- data.frame(sample = samples, patient = sub("[BL]$", "", samples),
                   tissue = ifelse(grepl("B$", samples), "peripheral blood", "lung"))
cells <- read_10x_contigs(setNames(contig_list, samples), meta = meta, by = "sample",
                          donor = patient)
```

The same data through scRepertoire gives the same table, except that
scRepertoire's `CTaa` does not record UMIs. For a cell with two alpha (or two
beta) chains, the first listed chain is used:

```{r screp, eval = has_screp}
comb <- scRepertoire::combineTCR(contig_list, samples = samples)
cells_s <- read_screpertoire(comb, donor = sub("[BL]$", "", sample))
```

## 2. Clones and paired TCRdist

```{r clones, eval = has_screp}
clones <- tcr_clones(cells)
clones
q <- top_public(cells, n = 10)
q[, c("rank", "va", "ca", "vb", "cb", "donors", "paired_donors", "concordance")]
hits <- tcrdist_paired(q, clones, radius = 108)
hits
```

`tcrdist_paired()` reproduces tcrdist3's human defaults (CDR1 + CDR2 + CDR2.5
of the V gene, plus 3 × CDR3 with 3 / 2 residues trimmed, BLOSUM62-based
mismatches, gap penalty 4 at the best position). The package tests check it
against tcrdist3 itself.

## 3. The figure

```{r fig1, eval = has_screp, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 8}
p <- hexrows(cells, aes(fill = tissue), queries = q, clones = clones) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("peripheral blood" = "#0072B2", lung = "#E69F00",
                               multiple = "#56B4E9"))
p
```

`ggsave_hexrows("rows.png", p)` saves it at 0.072 inch per hexagon unit with a
page sized to the rows and bins.

### Fill is any column, the ggplot way

There are no colour modes. Map any categorical expression:

* `aes(fill = sample)`, `aes(fill = paste(tissue, timepoint))`;
* cell-level values are summarised per clone by `summarise_fill`
  (`summarise_unique`: one value stays, several give `"multiple"`;
  `summarise_most_common`; or your own `function(values)`);
* the hexagons of a bin are banded in level order, so reorder with factor levels
  (`forcats::fct_relevel()`);
* without a scale, up to 8 fixed hues are used, then "Other" and "unknown",
  with clone counts in the legend; add any `scale_fill_*()` to change them.

### Tissue compartments

```{r tissue, eval = has_screp, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 5}
hexrows(cells, aes(fill = tissue_class(tissue), pattern = tissue_class(tissue)),
        queries = q[1:4, ], clones = clones, summarise_fill = summarise_tissue) +
  scale_fill_tissue() + scale_pattern_tissue()
```

`tissue_class()` maps free text to compartments by keyword (see
`tissue_rules()`). The tissue scales use Okabe-Ito colours plus textures
(stripes = gut, crosshatch = skin, dots = CNS / CSF), drawn by the package
itself, so ggpattern is not needed.

## 4. Your own queries

```{r query, eval = has_screp, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 2.6}
hexrows(cells, aes(fill = tissue),
        queries = c("rank-1 TCR again" = paste(q$va[1], q$ca[1], q$vb[1], q$cb[1], sep = ":")),
        clones = clones)
```

Queries are validated (V genes against the loop table, CDR3s must be amino
acids starting with C) before anything is computed.

## 5. HLA (synthetic data)

```{r hla, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 4.5}
cells2 <- tcrhex_example_cells(n_donors = 40)          # SYNTHETIC
cl2 <- tcr_clones(cells2)
q2 <- top_public(cells2, 3)
enr <- hla_enriched(tcrdist_paired(q2, cl2, radius = 24), cl2, radius = 24, queries = q2)
enr[, c("query", "allele", "k", "n", "p")]
q2$allele <- enr$allele
hexrows(cells2, aes(fill = hla_carrier(hla, .row_allele)), queries = q2, clones = cl2,
        row_tag = enr$text, title = "SYNTHETIC data: each row coloured by its own allele")
```

Every column of the query table is available in `aes()` as `.row_<column>`.

## 6. The data behind the figure

```{r data, eval = has_screp}
hd <- hexrows_data(cells, aes(fill = tissue), queries = q, clones = clones)
hd
head(hd$bins)   # row, bin, level, clones, shown
```
